summary: The note describes the Texas oil boom, which began with major petroleum strikes in Southeast Texas and spread to North Texas, East Texas, and the Permian Basin in West Texas. It highlights the 1901 Spindletop strike near Beaumont as the event that drew national attention and spurred exploration through the 1920s and beyond. It also names the Joiner strike in East Texas at the start of the Great Depression as one of the key strikes that launched this era.
one_line: Overview of the Texas oil boom, which started with strikes such as Spindletop in 1901 and spread across the state.
key_facts: The major petroleum strikes that began rapid growth in petroleum exploration and speculation in Texas occurred in Southeast Texas.
Reserves were soon found across Texas, and wells were constructed in North Texas, East Texas, and the Permian Basin in West Texas.
Limited reserves of oil had been struck in Texas during the 19th century.
The strike at Spindletop near Beaumont in 1901 gained national attention.
The Spindletop strike spurred exploration and development that continued through the 1920s and beyond.
The Joiner strike in East Texas occurred at the outset of the Great Depression.
Spindletop and the Joiner strike were described as the key strikes that launched the era of change in Texas.
The note is titled "Texas oil boom" and is sourced from Wikipedia.
